reasons: UNSUPPORTED: "Completed a master's in electrical engineering at Stanford 'mientras tanto' (while working)" (The NVIDIA bio confirms the Stanford MSEE but does not say when it was earned. 'While working' comes only from Britannica ('While working, he returned to school...'). Add [s:britannica] to this sentence.)
UNCITED: "'Dos décadas después cofundaba NVIDIA' (lede): about 21 years from age nine (c. 1972) to 1993. This is derived arithmetic and roughly correct, but uncited."
UNCITED: "'A los cinco años su familia se trasladó a Tailandia': supported by Britannica, but the sentence has no tag of its own."
UNCITED: "Summary, knownFor and FAQ answers have no inline citations. Their content is supported by sources already in person.json."

UNCITED: "The page never states his age, even though metaTitle promises 'edad' and 'jensen huang edad' is the first target query. As of 2026-10-26 he is 63 (born 1963-02-17 [s:britannica]). This must be added and cited."

Adds no value over existing pages: The facts are clean and use primary sources (the NVIDIA board bio and the CHM Fellow page), with no hype words or em dashes. The lede (nine years old, sent by mistake to a Kentucky reform school) is a strong, concrete opening. The page still fails the guide's main test. The first target query and the metaTitle promise 'edad', and the page never gives his age: there is no '63 años' and no '¿Cuántos años tiene Jensen Huang?' FAQ. A reader searching that has to work it out. The body is essentially a condensed version of the Britannica entry plus two lines from the NVIDIA bio, so it adds little a Spanish reader would not get from Wikipedia ES or Britannica. There is no Spanish-language source and no added local context. The story also stops in 2018, without the context (cited to CHM) that NVIDIA became one of the world's most valuable companies, which is why most people search him now.

Reviewer recommends rejection: Every factual claim checks out against nvidia-bio, britannica and chm, and both person.json facts (birth date and birthplace) are confirmed. A search confirms he is still NVIDIA CEO as of October 2026, so nothing is outdated. One citation is unsupported: the Stanford master's 'mientras tanto' is cited only to nvidia-bio, which gives no timing; add [s:britannica]. Rejected for value and search intent, not accuracy. Fixes: (1) State his age, 63 as of 2026-10-26 (born 17 February 1963 [s:britannica]), in the first screen and add a one-sentence FAQ '¿Cuántos años tiene Jensen Huang?'. Make sure the age will update or carries an as-of date. (2) Add [s:britannica] to the Stanford sentence and to 'A los cinco años... Tailandia'. (3) Consider 'reformatorio religioso' to match Britannica's 'reform school'. (4) Add something the top results lack, for example a short dated timeline, a Spanish-language source, or the post-2018 context from CHM on NVIDIA's position. Otherwise the page restates Britannica and should not be published.

claims.claim: Birth date: 17 February 1963 (person.json facts.birthDate, body, FAQ)
claims.note: Britannica gives 'born February 17, 1963, Tainan, Taiwan'.

claims.claim: Birthplace: Tainan, Taiwan (person.json facts.birthPlace, body, FAQ)
claims.note: Both sources say Tainan, Taiwan. CHM gives only the year 1963.

claims.claim: Born Jen-Hsun Huang
claims.note: Britannica: 'Also known as: Jen-Hsun Huang'.

claims.claim: The family moved to Thailand when he was five
claims.note: Britannica says so. The sentence has no citation of its own. It sits under the next sentence's [s:britannica], so add the tag here.

claims.claim: At about nine he and his brother were sent to an uncle in Tacoma, Washington, who enrolled them at the Kentucky school (Oneida Baptist Institute)
claims.note: Britannica confirms this, including that the uncle mistakenly thought it was a prestigious school.

claims.claim: Oneida Baptist Institute was a religious boarding school in Kentucky for 'difficult' children
claims.note: Britannica calls it a 'religious reform school for “difficult” children' in Oneida, Kentucky. 'Internado religioso' is acceptable, but 'reformatorio religioso' would be more exact.

claims.claim: At nine he came to the US from Thailand with his brother (lede, FAQ)
claims.note: Britannica covers the brother and the uncle. CHM: immigrated 'when he was nine years old'.

claims.claim: About two years later his parents arrived, took the boys out, and the family settled near Portland, Oregon
claims.note: Matches Britannica.

claims.claim: Finished high school in Aloha in 1981
claims.note: Britannica: attended Aloha High School, graduated in 1981.

claims.claim: BS in electrical engineering from Oregon State University, 1984
claims.note: Britannica confirms the 1984 BS in EE from OSU. The NVIDIA bio and CHM confirm the BSEE from OSU.

claims.claim: Met Lori Mills at OSU and married her
claims.note: Britannica: met Lori Mills, a fellow engineering student, and they later married. This is private life reported by a reliable outlet, so it is acceptable.

claims.claim: About a year at Advanced Micro Devices, then LSI Logic from 1985 to 1993
claims.note: NVIDIA bio: AMD 1984–1985, LSI Logic 1985–1993. Britannica: about a year at AMD.

claims.claim: Rose to run a division at LSI Logic
claims.note: Britannica: 'eventually become director of a company division'.

claims.claim: Completed a master's in electrical engineering at Stanford 'mientras tanto' (while working)
claims.note: The NVIDIA bio confirms the Stanford MSEE but does not say when it was earned. 'While working' comes only from Britannica ('While working, he returned to school...'). Add [s:britannica] to this sentence.

claims.claim: Co-founded NVIDIA in April 1993 with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, who chose him as CEO
claims.note: Britannica gives April 1993 and says the co-founders selected Huang as CEO. CHM gives 1993 and the same co-founders.

claims.claim: Started with $40,000; venture capital firms later put in $20 million
claims.note: Britannica: $40,000 capital, then an initial investment of $20 million from VC firms.

claims.claim: President, CEO and board member since the first day
claims.note: NVIDIA bio: 'has served since its inception as president, chief executive officer, and a member of the board of directors.' A web search shows he was still CEO in October 2026, so this is not outdated.

claims.claim: NVIDIA went public in 1999
claims.note: Britannica: 'The company went public in 1999.'

claims.claim: In 1999 it launched the GeForce 256, billed as the world's first GPU, combining transform, lighting and rendering
claims.note: CHM states it, including the transform, lighting and rendering detail. The article's hedge ('que anunció como') is appropriate.

claims.claim: CUDA was introduced in 2006 for general-purpose computing on NVIDIA GPUs
claims.note: Matches CHM.

claims.claim: AlexNet ran on NVIDIA GPUs in 2012, after which the company refocused on accelerated computing for AI
claims.note: CHM: after its GPUs powered AlexNet in 2012, the company 'pivoted again' to drive the modern era of AI with accelerated computing.

claims.claim: In 2018 Huang argued GPU performance was outpacing Moore's law, and the press called it 'Huang's law'
claims.note: Britannica cites the 2018 GTC in San Jose: GPUs 25 times faster than five years earlier, and the press named it 'Huang's law'.

claims.claim: Fortune Businessperson of the Year, 2017
claims.note: Confirmed by the NVIDIA bio and by Britannica.

claims.claim: Harvard Business Review named him the world's best-performing CEO in 2019
claims.note: NVIDIA bio: No. 1 on HBR's 2019 list of the world's 100 best-performing CEOs. Optionally add 'over the lifetime of their tenure' for precision.

claims.claim: Time 100 most influential people, 2021
claims.note: Matches Britannica.

claims.claim: Named a Computer History Museum Fellow in 2024
claims.note: The CHM page is headed '2024 Fellow'.

claims.claim: In 2007 he and his wife set up the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation
claims.note: Matches Britannica.

claims.claim: Summary/knownFor: Taiwan-born engineer, co-founded NVIDIA in 1993, has led it since as president and CEO; GeForce 256 in 1999 billed as the first GPU; AI computing focus since 2012
claims.note: Frontmatter has no citation tags, but every point is supported by nvidia-bio, britannica and chm as checked above.

claims.claim: FAQ: founded by Huang, Malachowsky and Priem in April 1993, with Huang chosen as CEO from the start
claims.note: Matches the sources.

claims.claim: FAQ: BS in EE from Oregon State in 1984, MS in EE from Stanford
claims.note: Matches the sources.
